title: The laundromat's machine
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The laundromat's copier: a dime a page, gray, the glass scratched. The strip comes out looking like a rumor of itself. Wood runs it anyway. The owner says it looks like the early ones. He says there are no early ones. She says there are now.

panels.composition: The laundromat's corner copier: coin slot, a scratched glass, a sign as blocks. WOOD feeding dimes. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a young man feeding dimes into a small scratched coin-operated copier in a laundromat corner, a small dog beside him, black and white, no words

panels.composition: A copy coming out: gray, streaked, the strip barely there. A rumor of a strip.

image.prompt: close on a gray streaked photocopy of a comic strip barely legible through the machine's scratches, black and white, no words
a laundromat owner holding a poor photocopy up to the light, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The copy, close: the scratches on the glass have become rain. The strip notices. The strip keeps them.

image.prompt: close on a gray photocopy where scratches on the copier glass read as streaks of rain across the drawing, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'There are now.' The scratches become rain; the strip keeps them for three weeks.
